SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl came upon the Prophet praying and forbade him, prompting the passage about the one who forbids a servant when he prays through the sinful, lying forelock.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r3.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاءه أبو جهل فنهاه فأنزل الله ﴿ أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾

BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.claim: The second conditional means that the forbidding man lies against the truth and turns from right guidance; its answer is the question whether he knows God sees.
BURSEVI:v10p365#2/r10.anchor: {أرءيت} أخبرني ذلك الناهي {إن كذب وتولى} أي إن

BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.claim: The second condition stands separately to signal that denial and turning away occur independently and bring the threat; the first supposition is impossible and merely broadens the comparison.
BURSEVI:v10p366/r13.anchor: فأمر مستحيل قد ذكر في حيز الشرط لتوسيع الدائرة وهو السر في تجريد الشرطية الأولى

QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.claim: If the arrogant man denied truth and turned from the straight religion in stubbornness, he should know God sees either state and will requite him.
QASHANI:96:9-14/r3.anchor: بالحق لكفره وأعرض عن الدين المستقيم لعناده وطغيانه

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r13.claim: The denier has denied the religion and turned away from guidance.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r13.anchor: أرءيت إن كذب وتولى } . كذب بالدين . وتولى عن الهداية

IBNASHUR:96:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:13/r1.claim: A fresh threat asks whether the person who denies and turns away supposes God is unaware of him; the first object of raʾayta is an omitted pronoun referring to the forbidding person.
IBNASHUR:96:13/r1.anchor: جملة مستأنفة للتهديد والوعيد على التكذيب والتولي

IBNASHUR:96:13/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:13/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR:96:13/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf takes “does he not know that God sees?” as the conditional answer, without the fa usually required before an interrogative answer.
IBNASHUR:96:13/r2.anchor: هو { ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى } كذا قدر صاحب « الكشاف »

IBNASHUR:96:13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:13/r3.speaker: الرضي
IBNASHUR:96:13/r3.claim: Al-Raḍī explicitly permits an interrogative conditional answer without fa, citing a parallel question in al-Anʿām.
IBNASHUR:96:13/r3.anchor: وصرح الرضي باختيار عدم اشتراط الاقتران بالفاء

IBNASHUR:96:13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:13/r4.claim: Most grammarians, including al-Zamakhsharī in al-Mufaṣṣal, require the answer to be joined by fa.
IBNASHUR:96:13/r4.anchor: جمهور النحاة والزمخشري في « المفصَّل » فهو وجوب الاقتران

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.claim: The clause begins a fresh threat: if the man denies the call and turns away, should he think God does not know what he does? The first object of “have you seen” is omitted and refers to the forbidding man.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r8.anchor: جملة مستأنفة للتهديد والوعيد على التكذيب والتولي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the question in verse 14 as the answer to the condition; al-Radi allows an interrogative answer without the expected fa, comparing another conditional question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r9.anchor: ولم يعتبر وجوب اقتران جملة جواب الشرط بالفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p447/r10.claim: Most grammarians, including al-Zamakhshari in al-Mufassal, require the fa; on their analysis the implicit answer is that God knows and will punish him, and verse 14 independently denies the offender’s ignorance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.claim: The conditional predicts that Abu Jahl will deny the Prophet when called to Islam and turn away; God promises to give the Prophet justice against him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r4.anchor: بأن أبا جهل سيكذبه حين يدعوه إلى الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.claim: The denial’s pronoun refers to the man who forbids prayer, while the object of “deny” is omitted because the preceding context identifies the servant he denies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p449/r5.anchor: وحذف مفعول { كذب } لدلالة ما قبله عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r5.claim: The one who lies and turns away is the man who forbids prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r5.anchor: وقوله: إن كذب وتولى، يعني الإنسان الذي ينهى،

AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.claim: The second arāʾayta clause in verse 13 is appositional to the first in verse 11, and the predicate is the statement in verse 14 that God sees.
AKHFASH:v2p582/r1.anchor: وجعل الخبر {ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى}

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r1.claim: The denier who turns away is the forbidding Abu Jahl.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra reads the question as asking what could be more astonishing than someone who forbids a servant from prayer while himself lying and turning away from remembrance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r2.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى وهو كاذب متول عن الذكر فأي شيء أعجب من هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari construes the phrase as asking whether the forbidding man is right.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p178#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري تقديره أرأيته مصيبا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.claim: God asks whether the forbidding opponent realizes that God sees and hears him, and will repay him fully for what he does.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r5.anchor: أي: أما علم هذا الناهي لهذا المهتدي أن الله يراه ويسمع كلامه، وسيجازيه على فعله أتم الجزاء.

FARRA:v3p278/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r6.claim: The conditional “if he denies and turns away” is an Arabic rhetorical formulation describing the one who forbids the servant as lying and turning away.
FARRA:v3p278/r6.anchor: وفيه عربية، مثله من الكلام لو قيل: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى وهو كاذب متول عن الذكر؟

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r12.claim: If the opponent denies God and His Messenger, turns away, and prevents worship, he will face punishment; this urges care in following truth.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r12.anchor: إن كذب الله ورسوله وتولى أعرض عن القبول ما يكون حاله في تكذيب المحق، والإعراض عن الحق،

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r9.claim: The passage threatens the disbeliever and shows that denial and turning away are human acts, not created by God.
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r9.anchor: ويدل قوله: (كذب وتولى) أن التكذيب فعله، ليس بخلق الله تعالى [*].

KASHSHAF:96:13/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:13/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:13/r1.claim: The alternative condition asks what if he denies the truth and turns from true religion, leading into the reminder that God sees.
KASHSHAF:96:13/r1.anchor: وكذلك إن كان على التكذيب للحق والتولي عن الدين الصحيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r9.claim: The challenge asks whether the forbidding person is rightly guided or commands piety, and whether he denies truth and turns away; God sees and repays both.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r9.anchor: أخبرني عمن ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته إن كان ذلك الناهي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r10.claim: The object of ara'ayta is the forbidding person with the conditional clauses; the first condition's omitted answer is supplied by the second, and the repeated ara'ayta is emphatic.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r10.anchor: الذي ينهى مع الجملة الشرطية ، وهما في موضع المفعولين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r12.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl for forbidding worship; if he does not stop, God will seize his forelock and drag him to Hell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r12.anchor: كلا } ردع لأبي جهل وخسوء له عن نهيه عن عبادة الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r4.claim: The denier and one who turns away is Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r4.anchor: أرأيت إن كذب وتولى } يعني أبا جهل , وفيه وجهان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r5.claim: Kadhdhaba wa-tawalla can mean he denied God and turned from obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r5.anchor: أحدهما : كذب بالله وتولى عن طاعته . الثاني : كذب بالقرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r6.claim: Alternatively, he denied the Quran and turned from faith.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r6.anchor: الثاني : كذب بالقرآن وتولى عن الإيمان . ويحتمل ثالثا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r7.claim: A further possibility is that he denied the Messenger and refused acceptance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p307/r7.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : كذب بالرسول وتولى عن القبول .

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.claim: The denier who turns away is Abū Jahl, who rejects the Qur'an; God sees both the Prophet alone and Abū Jahl's assembled company.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r3.anchor: يعني وأعرض { ألم يعلم } أبو جهل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#7/r1.claim: The question also asks whether this forbidding person denies the truth and turns away from it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#7/r1.anchor: أرأيت ان كان ذلك الناهى مكذبا بالحق متوليا عنه

NAHHAS:v5p261/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r14.claim: The verse refers to preventing prayer while denying God and His Messenger and turning from obedience.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r14.anchor: أي مع منعه من الصلاة أن كذب الله ورسوله وتولى عن طاعته

QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r1.claim: Abu Jahl rejected God's book and turned away from faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r1.anchor: يعني أبا جهل كذب بكتاب الله عز وجل، وأعرض عن الإيمان.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.claim: Al-Farra reads the three conditional questions together: the servant is guided and commands piety while the forbidding man denies and turns away, making his behavior astonishing; the question about God's seeing him confirms and rebukes, and each later ar'ayta may stand in place of the first.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:13-14/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى * عبدا إذا صلى } وهو على الهدى،

QUTB-ZILAL:96:13/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:13/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:13/r1.claim: The question adds a second, even more reprehensible act to the original offense: denial and turning away.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:13/r1.anchor: أضاف إلى الفعلة المستنكرة فعلة أخرى أشد نكرا

RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r1.claim: One reading addresses the Prophet: the preceding proofs are clear and reason shows it is wrong to stop a servant serving his Lord; one who denies them and obstructs worship acts in stubbornness, despite knowing God sees.
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r1.anchor: أنه خطاب مع الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ، وذلك لأن الدلائل التي ذكرها

RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r2.claim: The alternative addresses the unbeliever: if Muhammad is lying or turning away, would he not know that God sees him and stop, rather than need your prohibition?
RAZI-FULL:v32p22#2/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه خطاب للكافر ، والمعنى إن كان يا كافر محمد كاذبا

TAB:96:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:14/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:14/r2.claim: The three repetitions of araʾayta work by substitution; the sense is whether the forbidding, denying man knows that God sees him.
TAB:96:14/r2.anchor: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ،   أرأيت إن كان على الهدى } ،   فكررت أرأيت مرات ثلاثا على البدل

TAB-FULL:v24p535#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p535#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p535#2/r1.claim: Qatada identifies Abu Jahl as the one who denied and turned away.
TAB-FULL:v24p535#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {أرأيت إن كذب وتولى} [العلق: 13] : يعني: أبا جهل

TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.claim: The three repeated “Have you seen?” clauses are elliptical substitutions: the forbidding man is also a denier and turner-away, and must know that God sees him.
TAB-FULL:v24p536/r2.anchor: فكررت أرأيت مرات ثلاثا على البدل. والمعنى: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} [العلق: 9] ، وهو مكذب متول عن ربه، ألم يعلم بأن الله يراه

TABRISI:96:9-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:9-15/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:9-15/r6.claim: The one who denies and turns away is Abu Jahl, rejecting faith and refusing to listen.
TABRISI:96:9-15/r6.anchor: عن الإيمان وأعرض عن قبوله والإصغاء إليه

ASAD-NOTES:96:13#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:13#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:13#n7/r1.claim: The person turns from the truth because arrogance prevents him from facing it.
ASAD-NOTES:96:13#n7/r1.anchor: because in his arrogance he cannot face it

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#3/r1.claim: The liar who turns away from Islam is Abū Jahl; the clauses connect the worshipper's guidance and command to piety with the forbiddener's denial and rejection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#3/r1.anchor: ونظم هذه الآية على تقدير: أريت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى، وهو على الهدى، أمر بالتقوى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#3/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p175#3/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash explain the syntax as connected to what follows the repeated araʾayta, rather than treating the clauses as isolated.

WAHIDI-QT:96:13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:13/r1.claim: The verse asks about the astonishing case of a liar who turns from reminder forbidding someone who is guided and commands piety.
WAHIDI-QT:96:13/r1.anchor: وهو على الهدى آمر بالتقوى ،   والناهي كاذب متول عن الذكرى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r3.claim: Here ‘Have you seen?’ expresses astonishment; the linked questions contrast the guided, pious worshipper with a liar who turns away from the reminder.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r3.anchor: ومعنى: أرأيت ها هنا تعجب، وكذلك قوله:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r5.claim: The forbidding opponent denies the truth and turns away from the reminder, making the contrast astonishing.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r5.anchor: والناهي كاذب متول عن الذكرى، أي: فما أعجب من ذا!

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r1.claim: The author explains arayta as an attention-getting question meaning consider or tell me what you think; it usually rebukes, admonishes, or expresses amazement rather than seeking information.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r1.anchor: Onun için biz de yerine göre “gördün mü? Ne dersin? Söyle bakalım! Baksan a” diye terceme edegeldik.

ELMALILI:96:9-19/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r2.claim: The three questions may all address the Prophet or humanity, or alternate between disputants; the author finds the turn-taking debate more meaningful, though the first clearly addresses the Prophet and extends to everyone.
ELMALILI:96:9-19/r2.anchor: tarafeyn beyninde bir muhakeme veya bir hitâbet üslûbuyla sağa sola telvîn-i hitab olmak da kābil ve daha mânalıdır

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r13.claim: Addressing the Prophet, the question asks whether it is good for the prohibitor to deny the truth and turn away while the Prophet speaks truly.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r13.anchor: Peygamber’e hitab olduğuna göre şöyle demek olur: Baksana, yahut gördün a yâ Muhammed! Sen doğru olduğun, hakkı söylediğin hâlde

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r14.claim: Addressing the prohibitor, the alternative reading asks whether it would be good for the servant to obey him by denying truth, abandoning prayer, and turning away.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r14.anchor: Baksana, ey o kulu namazdan nehyeden azgın!

ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.speaker: Keşşâf
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.claim: Al-Kashshaf allows both conditional clauses to have expressed consequences, but the author prefers treating them as omitted and the following statement as an independent resumption.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#2/r17.anchor: Keşşâf’ın dediği gibi iki şartın ikisinin de cevâbı yapmak câiz olsa bile şartların cezâları mahzuf olarak bunun bir cümle-i istînâfiye olması daha muvâfıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.claim: A universal reading is more suitable: all tyrants in every age who obstruct religion's work of shaping social life by goodness, truth, and justice are criticized.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:9/r2.anchor: her dönemde görülen ve dinin sosyal hayatı iyilik, hak ve adalet ilkeleri yönünde şekillendirme işlevini engellemek isteyen bütün zorbaların eleştirildiği

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:13:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:13:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:13:anmerkung/r1.claim: Denying and turning away recur together in passages including 92:16, 79:21–22, and 75:32; related notes discuss the verbs kaḏḏaba and tawallā.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:13:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die Vorwürfe des „Leugnens“ (des Jüngsten Gerichts) und „Abwendens“ werden auch in 92:16

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r4.claim: The second possibility is that the blocker himself denied and turned away, making himself responsible for opening Hell’s door; the apodosis is suppressed to convey an unspeakable severity, a classical Arabic style.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p389/r4.anchor: Here, a suppression of the overall apodosis has occurred to point to the fact that its severity is beyond words

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r1.claim: The fate of those who deny and turn away is illustrated by 92:15–16, which says the wretched enter Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p390/r1.anchor: Only those wretched creatures shall enter Hell

QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#1/r1.claim: The canonical form among the Seven drops the medial hamza for a smoother pronunciation, with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#1/r1.anchor: drops the medial hamza, yielding a smoother pronunciation

QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#2/r1.claim: Hamza facilitation with a brief pause preserves the hamza's trace without full pronunciation.
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#2/r1.anchor: Hamza facilitation with sakt (brief pause at hamza position)

QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#3/r1.claim: The canonical madd lengthens ā before hamza and gives the interrogative additional rhythmic weight.
QIRAAT-ER:96:13:1#3/r1.anchor: lengthens the ā before the glottal stop, adding rhythmic weight to the interrogative

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.claim: The first raʾayta takes the relative clause as its first object; in the second and third clauses the first object is omitted as a pronoun or demonstrative referring back to the forbidding man.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r1.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه أو اسم إشارة يشار به إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p183#2/r2.claim: The third raʾayta's second object is the following clause, which the commentary introduces before continuing its grammatical analysis.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet while praying, but recoiled from a trench of fire, terror, and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb. The report is uncertain about whether the revelation was in Abu Hurayra's narration or another source.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r3.claim: The one who denies and turns away is Abu Jahl, turning away from faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r3.anchor: أرأيت إن كذب} يعني أبا جهل، {وتولى} عن الإيمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.claim: The rhetorical structure contrasts a guided servant who commands piety with a denier who turns away, exposing the strangeness of the persecutor's conduct.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p480#2/r4.anchor: وتقدير نظم الآية: أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى [والمنهي] (3) على الهدى، آمر بالتقوى، والناهي مكذب متول عن الإيمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.claim: The repeated أَرَأَيْتَ construction has the same grammatical function; its conditional is the second object, and its answer is omitted but supplied by the later condition. God sees the person's guidance and error.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r3.anchor: أرأيت تكرير للأول وكذا الذي في قوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.claim: One reading asks whether the forbidding person is himself guided and commands piety as he understands idol worship, or whether he is a denier who turns from truth; God sees all his states.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r4.anchor: إن كان ذلك الناهي على هدى فيما ينهى عنه، أو آمرا { بالتقوى }

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.claim: Another interpretation marvels that the worshipper is guided and commands piety while the forbidding person denies and turns away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r5.anchor: وقيل المعنى { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا } يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.claim: A further reading shifts the second question to the unbeliever, as if a judge addresses each of two litigants in turn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:9-14/r6.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.claim: Continuing al-Razi’s first solution, the rest of the surah came later about Abu Jahl, and the Prophet was directed to place these verses at its beginning.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r1.anchor: نزلت البقية في أبي جهل بن هشام، وأمر الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بضمها إلى أول السورة

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s second solution reads الإنسان generically: despite creation and blessings, people transgress, forget their return, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.anchor: أن تحمل الآيات على عموم لفظها في الظاهر، وهو أن الإنسان، جملة الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.claim: Both explanations are possible; the sequence suggests the passage followed public preaching and prayer, while a specific occasion does not prevent the wording from applying generally.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r3.anchor: وكلا الوجهين جائز. فسياق الآيات في السورة، يشعر بأنها نزلت بعد أن أبلغ المصطفى رسالة ربه

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the conditional clause in verse 13 the second object of arayta in verse 9, treats arayta before the condition as extra, and takes verse 14 as the condition’s answer.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r4.anchor: ذهب الزمخشري في (الكشاف) إلى أن الجملة الشرطية في {أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى}

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.claim: She objects that this analysis inserts an extra arayta into the flow and leaves an interrogative response unprefixed by fa, contrary to the grammarians’ rule.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r5.anchor: تبدو فيه {أَرَأَيْتَ} في الجملة الشرطية مقحمة على السياق، تمت للزمخشري تسوية الصنعة

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari’s analysis, holding that arayta’s second object must be an interrogative sentence, a construction frequent in the Quran.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r1.anchor: وكذلك رفض مذهب الزمخشري في جعل {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى} جواباً لشرط {إِنْ كَذَّبَ}

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan says an interrogative cannot answer a condition without fa except under poetic necessity, so he rejects al-Zamakhshari’s proposed answer.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r2.anchor: بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء في كل ما اقتضى طلباً بوجه ما، ولا يجوز حذفها إلا في ضرورة شعرية

BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.claim: She argues that Quranic interrogative arayta usually omits its second object and directs attention instead to the lesson or warning; she cites several Meccan examples.
BINTSHATI:v2p28/r3.anchor: وإنما يستغنى عن هذا المفعول، بتقرير يلفت إلى موضع العبرة والنذير

BINTSHATI:v2p29/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r1.claim: Plural araytum questions in al-Waqia about human emission, crops, drinking water, and fire follow the same pattern; she also cites other Meccan examples.
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r1.anchor: ومثلها السؤال التقريري، خطاباً للجمع، في آيات الواقعة

BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.claim: The repeated arayta in this passage is a stylistic prompt to see and reflect on the warning; it need not take an explicit or inferred second object.
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r2.anchor: فلفتت إلى ما هو جدير بالرؤية والبصر والتدبر، وأغنت عما تعلق به النجاة من مفعول ثان

BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.claim: Verse 14 itself supplies the focal lesson in place of an assumed conditional answer: knowing that God sees is the needed warning, without a hidden answer clause.
BINTSHATI:v2p29/r3.anchor: لتكون آية {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى} هو موضع العبرة والبصر والتنبيه

BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.claim: Other Quranic conditional questions are followed by interrogatives without fa, including examples in al-Anam, al-Qasas, and Hud.
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r1.anchor: والاستفهام فيها في موضع حواب الشرط، غير مقترن بالفاء

BINTSHATI:v2p30/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says raʾa with two objects can mean knowing, and arayta functions like akhbirni; such questions alert the listener to a warning.
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r2.anchor: رأى إذا عدى إلى مفعولين اقتضى معنى العلم. ويجرى {أَرَأَيْتَ} مجرى: أخبرني

BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.claim: She urges readers to notice Quranic stylistic patterns even when they depart from school grammar and rhetoric, rather than forcing them into technical rules by conjecture.
BINTSHATI:v2p30/r3.anchor: فيشغلنا عن البيان العالى، تسوية الصنعة النحوية أو البلاغية، بالتأويل فيه والتقدير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r5.claim: If the forbiddener denies that the praying servant is guided and turns away from accepting piety, the omitted answer is that such baseless denial and turning away are plainly evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p484/r5.anchor: والجواب محذوف تقديره : ألم يكن ذلك التولي والتكذيب شرا له

DURR:96:6/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:6/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:6/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:7/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:7/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:7/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:7/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:9/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:9/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:9/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:9/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:10/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:10/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:10/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:10/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:15/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:15/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:15/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:15/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:16/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:16/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:16/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:16/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.claim: He says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad; the guided one is Muhammad, the denier is Abu Jahl, his assembly is his clan, and ‘zabaniya’ means police in Arabic.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} قال: نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

TAB:96:13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:13/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:13/r1.claim: The question concerns Abu Jahl: if he denies the truth Muhammad brought and turns away from it, he does not believe.
TAB:96:13/r1.anchor: أرأيت إن كذب أبو جهل بالحق الذي بعث به محمدا وتولى ،   يقول :  وأدبر عنه

TAB:96:13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:13/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:13/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the denier who turns away as Abu Jahl.
TAB:96:13/r2.anchor: عن قتادة { أرأيت إن كذب وتولى } يعني :  أبا جهل

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r5.claim: The apparent addressee of both instances of “Have you seen?” is the Messenger; the pronoun sequence supports this reading.
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r5.anchor: والخطاب في { أرأيت } الظاهر أنه للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ، وكذا { أرأيت } الثاني ، والتناسق في الضمائر هو الذي يقتضيه النظم

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.claim: Another view addresses the unbeliever: would he forbid the worshipper if the prayer were guidance, calling to God, and commanding piety?
ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r6.anchor: وقيل : { أرأيت } خطاب للكافر التفت إلى الكافر فقال : أرأيت يا كافر ، إن كانت صلاته هدى ودعاء إلى الله وأمراً بالتقوى

ABUHAYYAN:96:11/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān

ALUSI:96:10/r20.speaker: قيل

ALUSI:96:10/r20.anchor: والرؤية قيل قلبية وكذا في قوله تعالى : { أَرَءيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وتولى }

ALUSI:96:10/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r23.claim: The answers to the two conditional clauses are omitted, with “Does he not know?” supplying the indication; another view takes “Have you seen?” as their cue.
ALUSI:96:10/r23.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه

ALUSI:96:10/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r24.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r24.claim: An alternative says the conditional answers are indicated by “Have you seen?”, understood as referring to what will soon be stated.
ALUSI:96:10/r24.anchor: وقيل يدل عليه أرأيت مراداً به ما سيذكر قريباً

ALUSI:96:10/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r25.claim: In the principal parsing, the unexpressed subjects of “was” and the following verbs refer to the prohibiter.
ALUSI:96:10/r25.anchor: والضمائر المستترة في { كان } وما بعد من الأفعال للناهي

ALUSI:96:10/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r31.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r31.claim: The clauses are separated to intensify rebuke and warning and show that each has an independent point.
ALUSI:96:10/r31.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

ALUSI:96:10/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r34.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r34.claim: Finally it warns him on the actual premise that he denies prayer’s truth and turns away from it.
ALUSI:96:10/r34.anchor: وشنع جل شأنه عليه ثالثاً بذلك وأوعده عليه أيضاً على تقدير أنه في نفس الأمر

ALUSI:96:10/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r35.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r35.claim: The sequence rises in severity: a general warning, one framed around the prohibiter’s claimed position, then one about his actual position.
ALUSI:96:10/r35.anchor: وهذا كالترقي في التشنيع والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا

ALUSI:96:10/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r36.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:10/r36.claim: The majority read the first condition as a supposedly righteous course in forbidding worship of God or commanding piety while calling to idols, and the next as the prohibiter’s actual denial and turning away.
ALUSI:96:10/r36.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة

ALUSI:96:10/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r37.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:10/r37.claim: The majority treat the second condition as repeating the first, since the first already implies lack of guidance; the conditional wording feigns concession and taunts, with the second taunt reversing the first.
ALUSI:96:10/r37.anchor: وذكر أن الشرط الثاني تكرار للأول لأن معنى الأول أنه ليس على الهدى

ALUSI:96:10/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r38.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r38.claim: An alternative makes the first seeing visual and needing no second object, but the second and third inward; their conditional clauses fill the second-object position.
ALUSI:96:10/r38.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان

ALUSI:96:10/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r39.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r39.claim: In that parsing, the final question is unjoined to signal its independent actual occurrence and ensuing threat; the earlier condition only broadens the case and refers to the later answer.
ALUSI:96:10/r39.anchor: ولم تعطف الأخيرة على ما قبلها للإيذان باستقلالها بالوقوع في نفس الأمر

ALUSI:96:10/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r40.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r40.claim: Another analysis takes all three questions as inward seeing: the first conditional’s answer is omitted in favor of the second’s, while the third question independently opposes the first condition.
ALUSI:96:10/r40.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI:96:10/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r41.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r41.claim: Al-Ālūsī objects that these analyses allow an interrogative conditional answer without the required fāʾ.
ALUSI:96:10/r41.anchor: إن في تجويز الإتيان بالاستفهام في جزاء الشرط من غير الفاء

ALUSI:96:10/r43.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r43.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:10/r43.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says he knows no one who permits an interrogative conditional answer without fāʾ; grammarians require it for any clause expressing a request, except in necessity or poetry.
ALUSI:96:10/r43.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه

ALUSI:96:10/r45.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r45.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI:96:10/r45.claim: Al-Khafājī replies that the conditional and interrogative clauses may figuratively occupy the object and answer positions because they indicate those meanings; al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī state this explicitly.
ALUSI:96:10/r45.anchor: وقال الخفاجي إن جعل الشرطية في موقع المفعول والجملة الاستفهامية في موقع جواب الشرط

ALUSI:96:10/r46.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r46.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r46.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the second object of “Have you seen?” must only be an interrogative clause, noting that this conflicts with what is reported as Sibawayh’s chosen view.
ALUSI:96:10/r46.anchor: مخالف لما صرحوا بأنه مختار سيبويه فلا يلتفت إليه

ALUSI:96:10/r47.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r47.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r47.claim: Some exclude both prohibiter and worshipper from the address on contextual grounds; al-Baḥr prefers the Prophet as addressee, while others allow the disbeliever, with the scene cast generally.
ALUSI:96:10/r47.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي لأن السياق مقتض لخروج الناهي والمنهي

ALUSI:96:10/r48.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r48.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:10/r48.claim: Al-Farrāʾ’s reading makes the worshipper the subject of the second condition and the prohibiter the subject of the third: the worshipper is guided and commands piety, while the prohibiter denies and turns away—how astonishing.
ALUSI:96:10/r48.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً يصلي والمنهي على الهدى وأمر بالتقوى

ALUSI:96:10/r49.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r49.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r49.claim: On al-Farrāʾ’s reading the omitted answer is “How astonishing this is”; the connective aw is taken as waw, and “Have you seen?” may mean inward knowledge or literal sight.
ALUSI:96:10/r49.anchor: والظاهر أن جواب الشرط عليه محذوف وهو فما أعجب من ذا بقرينة أرأيت

ALUSI:96:10/r50.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r50.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:10/r50.claim: One view splits the address between the disbeliever and the Messenger, like a judge speaking to opposing litigants.
ALUSI:96:10/r50.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في أرأيت الثانية للكافر وفي الثانية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:96:10/r54.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r54.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:10/r54.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9–10 as exposing tyranny when a person feels self-sufficient, 96:11–12 as rebuking lost guidance and piety, and 96:13–14 as rebuking earned punishment and distance from God.
ALUSI:96:10/r54.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:10/r55.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:10/r55.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:10/r55.claim: Al-Ālūsī distances himself from ʿIṣām al-Dīn’s elaboration, inviting reflection and leaving the matter to God’s intended meaning.
ALUSI:96:10/r55.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:11/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r14.claim: On one syntactic analysis, the first object of the first arāʾayta is the relative clause; the corresponding objects in the next two are elided, while their second object is ألم يعلم. The earlier conditional answers are omitted and inferred from that answer.
ALUSI:96:11/r14.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه أو اسم إشارة يشار به إليه

ALUSI:96:11/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads a three-stage rebuke: first the ban on prayer is condemned without regard to the forbidd er's claimed or actual state; then it is condemned even if he claims guidance or urges piety; finally it is condemned given his actual denial and turning away, with divine sight and punishment underscoring each stage.
ALUSI:96:11/r16.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي ثم شنع وأوعد جل وعلا عليه مع التعرض لحاله الزعمي

ALUSI:96:11/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r17.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:11/r17.claim: The majority do not restrict the conditions to al-Ālūsī's layered stages: being guided while forbidding worship or urging piety while commanding idolatry is impossible, so the conditional wording feigns concession and mocks the forbidding man; the next condition restates the point as his certain denial and turning away.
ALUSI:96:11/r17.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه

ALUSI:96:11/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r18.claim: An alternative takes the first arāʾayta as visual and the next two as mental; the relative is the first object's antecedent, the last object is ألم يعلم, and the middle object is supplied from it. The last clause is uncoordinated to mark its actual occurrence and ensuing threat.
ALUSI:96:11/r18.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان وفي الثانية والثالثة قلبية

ALUSI:96:11/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r19.claim: Another analysis makes all three arāʾayta mental: the first takes the first conditional and its omitted answer as its second object, the second repeats the first, and the third independently contrasts with it; ألم يعلم answers the second condition while the first answer is omitted.
ALUSI:96:11/r19.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول ومفعولها الثاني الجملة الشرطية الأولى

ALUSI:96:11/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:11/r20.claim: A further view treats the second and third arāʾayta as repetitions of the first; both conditions fill its second-object position, ألم يعلم answers the second, and the first answer is omitted because the later one makes it understood.
ALUSI:96:11/r20.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى والشرطيتان بجوابهما سادتان مسد المفعول الثاني

ALUSI:96:11/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r21.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:11/r21.claim: A grammatical objection says the conditional clause cannot itself be the second object of arāʾayta, which Abū Ḥayyān and others require to be interrogative (or, as in al-Irshād, oath-like).
ALUSI:96:11/r21.anchor: واعترض أيضاً جعل الجملة الشرطية في موضع المفعول الثاني لا رأيت بأن مفعولها الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية كمانص عليه أبو حيان وجماعة

ALUSI:96:11/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r22.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:11/r22.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that a conditional answer expressed as an interrogative requires fa; he says no one permits omitting it except in necessity or poetry. Al-Damāmīnī likewise finds the proposed parsing of هل يهلك in 6:47 problematic without fa.
ALUSI:96:11/r22.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء

ALUSI:96:11/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r23.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI:96:11/r23.claim: Al-Khafājī answers that the conditional and interrogative clauses can together occupy the object and answer positions, either directly or by implication; al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī say this accords with Sībawayh's preferred analysis.
ALUSI:96:11/r23.anchor: وقال الخفاجي إن جعل الشرطية في موقع المفعول والجملة الاستفهامية في موقع جواب الشرط إما على ظاهره

ALUSI:96:11/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r27.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:11/r27.claim: Al-Farrāʾ instead assigns the pronouns in كان and أمر to the praying servant, and those in كذب وتولى and يعلم to the forbidding man: the servant is guided and urges piety, while his opponent denies and turns away.
ALUSI:96:11/r27.anchor: وقيل الضميران في أن كان وأمر للعبد المصلي والضمائر في كذب وتولى ويعلم للذي ينهى وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء

ALUSI:96:11/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:11/r32.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:11/r32.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as evidence of the tyrant's arrogance when self-sufficient, 96:11 as reproach for losing the benefit of guidance and piety, 96:13 as reproach for earning punishment, and ألم يعلم as a severe threat.
ALUSI:96:11/r32.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:12/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r15.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r15.claim: Some take the vision in the first and third questions as intellectual rather than visual; grammarians hold two views on this construction.
ALUSI:96:12/r15.anchor: والرؤية قيل قلبية وكذا في قوله تعالى : { أَرَءيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وتولى }

ALUSI:96:12/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r17.claim: In one parsing, the first question’s object is the relative clause, while those of the second and third are omitted pronouns or demonstratives; the third question’s second object is ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى.
ALUSI:96:12/r17.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه أو اسم إشارة يشار به إليه

ALUSI:96:12/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r18.claim: The answers to the two conditional clauses are omitted, with ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى indicating them; another analysis lets arayta indicate the answer.
ALUSI:96:12/r18.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه ويقدر حسبما تقتضيه الصناعة

ALUSI:96:12/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:12/r23.claim: Al-Ālūsī reads three escalating reproaches: first for forbidding prayer without regard to the forbidder’s state, then on the state he claims, and finally on his actual denial and turning away, each ending in divine threat.
ALUSI:96:12/r23.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي ثم شنع وأوعد جل وعلا عليه مع التعرض لحاله الزعمي

ALUSI:96:12/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r24.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:12/r24.claim: The majority read the conditions as ironic concessions: the forbidder is supposedly guided or enjoining piety while calling to idols, yet in truth denies the truth and turns away; both conditions return to one point.
ALUSI:96:12/r24.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا حيث قالوا إن كان على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله تعالى

ALUSI:96:12/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r25.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r25.claim: One parsing makes the first question visual and the next two intellectual; the conditional clauses fill the second-object position, while the uncoordinated final clause stresses its occurrence and threat.
ALUSI:96:12/r25.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان وفي الثانية والثالثة قلبية

ALUSI:96:12/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r26.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r26.claim: A further parsing takes all three questions as intellectual: the first relative clause is its first object, the first conditional supplies its second object through an omitted answer, and the third question stands independently.
ALUSI:96:12/r26.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول ومفعولها الثاني الجملة الشرطية الأولى بجوابها المحذوف

ALUSI:96:12/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r27.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r27.claim: Another account treats the second and third arayta as repetitions of the first; both conditions occupy its second-object position, ألم يعلم answers the second, and the first answer is omitted as understood.
ALUSI:96:12/r27.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى والشرطيتان بجوابهما سادتان مسد المفعول الثاني للأولى

ALUSI:96:12/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r28.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:96:12/r28.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows an interrogative clause to answer a conditional without fa, citing 6:47; Abū Ḥayyān says a request clause requires fa except in poetic or necessary usage.
ALUSI:96:12/r28.anchor: وإن صرح له الزمخشري في كشافه وارتضاه الرضي واستشهد له بقوله تعالى : { قل أرأيتم

ALUSI:96:12/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r29.speaker: الدماميني
ALUSI:96:12/r29.claim: Al-Damāmīnī says treating هل يهلك as the conditional answer is problematic because it lacks the required fa.
ALUSI:96:12/r29.anchor: وقال الدماميني في شرح التسهيل إن جعل هل يهلك جزاء مشكل لعدم اقترانه بالفاء

ALUSI:96:12/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r30.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:12/r30.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and other grammarians object that a conditional clause cannot be the second object of arayta, which they restrict to an interrogative or oath clause.
ALUSI:96:12/r30.anchor: واعترض أيضاً جعل الجملة الشرطية في موضع المفعول الثاني لا رأيت بأن مفعولها الثاني لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية

ALUSI:96:12/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r31.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI:96:12/r31.claim: Al-Khafājī replies that the conditional may literally be the object and the interrogative its answer, or both may be treated so because together they convey those meanings.
ALUSI:96:12/r31.anchor: وقال الخفاجي إن جعل الشرطية في موقع المفعول والجملة الاستفهامية في موقع جواب الشرط إما على ظاهره

ALUSI:96:12/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r32.speaker: الرضي
ALUSI:96:12/r32.claim: Al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī say restricting arayta’s second object to an interrogative clause conflicts with the analysis explicitly preferred by Sībawayh.
ALUSI:96:12/r32.anchor: فما قيل من أن المفعول الثاني لا رأيت لا يكون إلا جملة استفهامية مخالف لما صرحوا بأنه مختار سيبويه

ALUSI:96:12/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r33.speaker: البحر
ALUSI:96:12/r33.claim: Earlier interpreters do not address the Prophet or the unbelieving forbidder, since context removes both from the address; al-Baḥr favors the Prophet, while another view permits addressing the unbeliever.
ALUSI:96:12/r33.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي لأن السياق مقتض لخروج الناهي والمنهي عن مورد الخطاب

ALUSI:96:12/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r34.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:12/r34.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns كان and أمر to the praying servant, but كذب and تولى and يعلم to the forbidder: the servant is guided and enjoins piety while the forbidder denies and turns away.
ALUSI:96:12/r34.anchor: وقيل الضميران في أن كان وأمر للعبد المصلي والضمائر في كذب وتولى ويعلم للذي ينهى وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء

ALUSI:96:12/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r35.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:12/r35.claim: One view alternates addresses, asking the unbeliever whether he would forbid prayer that guides and calls to piety, then asking the Prophet whether the denier knows God sees him.
ALUSI:96:12/r35.anchor: وقيل الخطاب في أرأيت الثانية للكافر وفي الثانية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو عز وجل كالحاكم الذي حضر الخصمان

ALUSI:96:12/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:12/r39.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:12/r39.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as exposing tyranny born of self-sufficiency, 96:11 as reproaching lost guidance and piety, 96:13 as reproaching earned punishment and distance from God, and 96:14 as the threat after both reproaches.
ALUSI:96:12/r39.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r1.claim: The passage from 96:9 onward recounts some consequences of human tyranny and threatens the one who prevents prayer.
ALUSI:96:13/r1.anchor: ذكر لبعض آثار الطغيان ووعيد عليها

ALUSI:96:13/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r15.claim: The future-form wording evokes the past scene as something strange and astonishing.
ALUSI:96:13/r15.anchor: والتعبير بما يفيد الاستقبال لاستحضار الصورة الماضية لنوع غرابة

ALUSI:96:13/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r16.claim: Here raʾayta means “tell me”: since seeing leads to knowledge, asking about seeing functions as asking about its object; grammarians have two analyses of this usage.
ALUSI:96:13/r16.anchor: والمراد من أرأيت أخبرني فإن الرؤية لما كانت سبباً للعلم

ALUSI:96:13/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r17.claim: In the principal parse, the first raʾayta takes the relative clause as its first object; the second and third have an omitted first object referring back, and the third’s second object is “does he not know that God sees?”
ALUSI:96:13/r17.anchor: والمفعول الأول للأول الموصول وللثاني والثالث محذوف وهو ضمير يعود عليه

ALUSI:96:13/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r18.claim: The apparent ellipsis here is semantic request, not tanāzuʿ: clauses cannot be elided as competing syntactic governors; al-Ālūsī illustrates with a report about Zayd.
ALUSI:96:13/r18.anchor: وليس ذلك من التنازع لأن الجمل لا يصح إضمارها وإنما هو من الطلب المعنوي

ALUSI:96:13/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r19.claim: The answers to both conditional clauses are omitted, with 96:14 indicating them; another parse takes raʾayta itself to point to the answer soon to be stated.
ALUSI:96:13/r19.anchor: وجواب الشرط في الجملتين محذوف لدلالة ألم يعلم عليه

ALUSI:96:13/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r20.claim: The address in all three questions may be to anyone capable of understanding; another view takes it as addressing humankind, as in “to your Lord” at 96:8.
ALUSI:96:13/r20.anchor: والخطاب في الكل على ما اختاره جمع لكل من يصلح أن يكون مخاطباً

ALUSI:96:13/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r24.claim: The clauses are separated to intensify censure and threat, presenting each as independently deserving condemnation.
ALUSI:96:13/r24.anchor: وفصل بين الجمل للاعتناء بأمر التشنيع والوعيد حيث أشعر أن كل جملة مقصودة على حيالها

ALUSI:96:13/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r25.claim: The passage escalates: first it condemns forbidding prayer without regard to the forbidding person’s supposed status, then condemns it if he claims guidance, then if he actually denies prayer’s truth and turns away.
ALUSI:96:13/r25.anchor: والحاصل أنه تعالى شنع وأوعد على النهي عن الصلاة بدون تعرض لحال الناهي الزعمي أو الحقيقي

ALUSI:96:13/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r26.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:13/r26.claim: The majority do not limit the conditionals as al-Ālūsī did: the first supposes guidance or enjoining piety as claimed, the second denial and turning away as the commentators affirm.
ALUSI:96:13/r26.anchor: والجمهور على عدم تقييد ما في حيز الشرطيتين بما ذكرنا

ALUSI:96:13/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r27.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI:96:13/r27.claim: For the majority, the conditional form feigns latitude and taunts: there can be no guidance in forbidding worship of God and ordering idol worship, while the denier plainly is astray; both conditions return to one point.
ALUSI:96:13/r27.anchor: إذ لا يكون في النهي عن عبادته تعالى والأمر بعبادة الأصنام هدى البتة

ALUSI:96:13/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r28.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r28.claim: One parse makes the first raʾayta visual, needing no second object, and the second and third cognitive, with their conditional clauses and answers filling the second-object position.
ALUSI:96:13/r28.anchor: وقيل إن الرؤية في الجملة الأولى بصرية فلا تحتاج إلى مفعول ثان

ALUSI:96:13/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r29.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r29.claim: Another parse treats all three as cognitive: the first takes the relative clause as object one, its condition as object two, and the third omits object one while explicitly supplying the threatening answer.
ALUSI:96:13/r29.anchor: وقيل إن أرأيت في الجمل الثلاث من الرؤية القلبية والمفعول الأول للأولى الموصول

ALUSI:96:13/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r30.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r30.claim: In that parse, the final clause is unjoined to reinforce the rebuke and signal the condition’s truth; stating its answer makes the threat explicit, while the first conditional’s answer is understood from the second.
ALUSI:96:13/r30.anchor: وفي الإتيان بالجملة الأخيرة من دون العطف ترشيح للكلام المبكت وتنبيه على حقية الشرط

ALUSI:96:13/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r31.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r31.claim: A further parse makes the second and third raʾayta repetitions of the first; both conditionals fill its second-object slot, 96:14 answers the second, and the first answer is omitted by analogy.
ALUSI:96:13/r31.anchor: وقيل أرأيت في الجملتين الثانية والثالثة تكرار للأولى

ALUSI:96:13/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r32.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:13/r32.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that an interrogative sentence cannot answer a conditional without faʾ; he says grammarians require it whenever the answer expresses a request, except in poetic necessity.
ALUSI:96:13/r32.anchor: وقال أبو حيان إن وقوع جملة الاستفهام جواباً للشرط بغير فاء لا أعلم أحد أجازه

ALUSI:96:13/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r33.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:13/r33.claim: Abū Ḥayyān and others object that raʾayta’s second object must be an interrogative or oath clause; al-Khafājī answers that the condition and question together can fill that slot.
ALUSI:96:13/r33.anchor: إلا جملة استفهامية كمانص عليه أبو حيان وجماعة أو قسمية

ALUSI:96:13/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r34.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI:96:13/r34.claim: Al-Khafājī says the conditional and its interrogative answer may be taken literally together as raʾayta’s second object, or treated as filling it together because they jointly indicate that object; al-Raḍī and al-Damāmīnī also state this.
ALUSI:96:13/r34.anchor: وقال الخفاجي إن جعل الشرطية في موقع المفعول والجملة الاستفهامية في موقع جواب الشرط

ALUSI:96:13/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r35.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r35.claim: The prohibitor and worshipper are outside the addressee role in the immediate context; al-Baḥr prefers addressing the Prophet, while another permits addressing the unbelieving prohibitor in a generic scene.
ALUSI:96:13/r35.anchor: ولم يجعلوا فيما ذكر الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا للكافر الناهي

ALUSI:96:13/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r36.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:96:13/r36.claim: Al-Farrāʾ assigns “was” and “commanded” to the praying servant, but “denied,” “turned away,” and “knows” to the prohibitor; the implied conclusion is how astonishing the case is.
ALUSI:96:13/r36.anchor: وحاصل المعنى على ما قال الفراء أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً يصلي والمنهي على الهدى

ALUSI:96:13/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r37.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:13/r37.claim: Another proposal shifts the second question’s addressee to the disbeliever and the third’s to the Prophet, like a judge addressing two litigants; its “or” is division equivalent to “and.”
ALUSI:96:13/r37.anchor: فهو عز وجل كالحاكم الذي حضر الخصمان يخاطب هذا مرة والآخر أخرى

ALUSI:96:13/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r41.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:96:13/r41.claim: The Imam reads the condition as asking whether a sensible, wealthy man would not do better to seek guidance and command piety than disbelieve and prohibit worship; God laments his forfeiture of high ranks for low ones.
ALUSI:96:13/r41.anchor: وجوز الإمام كون الخطاب في الكل له عليه الصلاة والسلام وقال في بيان معنى

ALUSI:96:13/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r42.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:13/r42.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn reads 96:9 as tyranny born of self-sufficiency, 96:11–12 as rebuke for forfeiting guidance and piety, and 96:13 as rebuke for earning punishment and distance from God; 96:14 is a severe threat.
ALUSI:96:13/r42.anchor: واعتبر عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r45.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r45.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:96:13/r45.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn takes the final question as rebuke for earned harm: denial and turning away merit punishment and distance from the Lord, followed by a severe threat.
ALUSI:96:13/r45.anchor: عصام الدين هذه الجملة توبيخاً على تفويت ما ينفع وما بعدها توبيخاً على كسب ما يضر

ALUSI:96:13/r46.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r46.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r46.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls ʿIṣām al-Dīn’s overall reading far-fetched and leaves the intent to God after reviewing the preceding analyses.
ALUSI:96:13/r46.anchor: وهو كما ترى فتأمل جميع ما تقدم والله تعالى بمراده أعلم

ALUSI:96:13/r47.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:13/r47.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:13/r47.claim: Although revealed about Abū Jahl, the threat applies to everyone who prohibits prayer; this does not forbid objecting to prayer in usurped places or disliked times, since the objection concerns a concomitant quality, not prayer itself.
ALUSI:96:13/r47.anchor: ثم إن الآية وإن نزلت في أبي جهل عليه اللعنة لكن كل من نهى عن الصلاة ومنع منها فهو شريكه في الوعيد

BAGHAWI:96:13/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:13/r1.claim: The one who denies is Abu Jahl, and turning away means turning away from faith.
BAGHAWI:96:13/r1.anchor: أرأيت إن كذب } يعني أبا جهل ، { وتولى } عن الإيمان

BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.claim: The sentence contrasts the forbidden servant, who is guided and commands piety, with the forbidding man, who denies and turns away; Baghawi calls the contrast astonishing.
BAGHAWI:96:13/r2.anchor: وتقدير نظم الآية : أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى ، والمنهي على الهدى ، آمر بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول عن الإيمان

BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.claim: The conditional is the second object of Have you considered; its answer is omitted and supplied by the answer to the second conditional, which serves as its counterpart.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r1.anchor: والشرطية مفعوله الثاني ، وجواب الشرط محذوف دل عليه جواب الشرط الثاني الواقع موقع القسيم له

BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.claim: He asks about the one forbidding a servant’s prayer: is the forbidding man guided or enjoining piety as he believes in idol worship, or denying truth and turning from right? God sees each one’s guidance and error.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r2.anchor: أو آمرا بالتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقده ، أو إن كان على التكذيب للحق والتولي عن الصواب كما تقول

BAYDAWI:96:13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI:96:13/r3.claim: One interpretation contrasts a praying servant who is guided and enjoining piety with a forbidding man who denies truth and turns away, and marvels at the situation.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r3.anchor: وقيل : المعنى أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا يصلي ، والمنهي على الهدى آمرا بالتقوى ، والناهي مكذب متول ، فما أعجب من ذا

BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.claim: Another interpretation makes the second address speak to the unbeliever, as a judge addresses two litigants in turn: would he forbid prayer that guides and calls to God?
BAYDAWI:96:13/r4.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب في الثانية مع الكافر ، فإنه سبحانه وتعالى كالحاكم الذي حضره الخصمان : يخاطب هذا مرة

BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.claim: Piety is mentioned in the rebuke but not the prohibition because the prohibition concerned prayer and the command to piety; prayer alone suffices as an active call.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r5.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ، ولم يتعرض له في النهي ؛ لأن النهي كان عن الصلاة والأمر بالتقوى

BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.claim: Alternatively, forbidding a praying servant may concern prayer or other matters; people’s states are encompassed by perfecting oneself through worship and others through calling them.
BAYDAWI:96:13/r6.anchor: أو لأن نهي العبد إذا صلى يحتمل أن يكون لها ولغيرها وعامة أحوالها محصورة في تكميل نفسه بالعبادة وغيره بالدعوة

BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.claim: The conditional is the second object of Have you considered; its answer is omitted and supplied by the answer to the second conditional, which serves as its counterpart.
BAYDAWI:96:14/r1.anchor: والشرطية مفعوله الثاني ، وجواب الشرط محذوف دل عليه جواب الشرط الثاني الواقع موقع القسيم له

BAYDAWI:96:14/r2.speaker: author

BAYDAWI:96:14/r4.speaker: قيل

BAYDAWI:96:14/r5.anchor: ولعله ذكر الأمر بالتقوى في التعجب والتوبيخ ، ولم يتعرض له في النهي ؛ لأن النهي كان

BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.claim: Alternatively, forbidding a praying servant may concern prayer or other matters; people’s states are encompassed by perfecting oneself through worship and others through calling them.
BAYDAWI:96:14/r6.anchor: أو لأن نهي العبد إذا صلى يحتمل أن يكون لها ولغيرها وعامة أحوالها محصورة في تكميل نفسه بالعبادة وغيره بالدعوة

BIQAI:96:13/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:13/r1.claim: The inferred responses to the preceding questions lead to a further rebuke: the repeated interrogative introduces a state opposed to guidance and heightens reproach and astonishment.

BIQAI:96:13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:13/r2.claim: The forbidding person denies that the worshipper is guided by serving the universally acknowledged Lord, thereby committing manifest misguidance driven only by desire.
BIQAI:96:13/r2.anchor: بأن المصلي على الهدى بخدمة سيده المتفق على سيادته

BIQAI:96:13/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:13/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:13/r3.claim: Turning away forcibly redirects the person's original nature from accepting taqwa and ruins his inner character and outward conduct; the omitted response is that such denial and turning away are evil, especially against the evidence.
BIQAI:96:13/r3.anchor: وكلف فطرته الأولى بعد معالجتها الإعراض عن قبول الأمر بالتقوى

BIQAI:96:15/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:15/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:15/r2.claim: In the author's ihtibāk analysis, the second question omits being astray, inferred from the earlier guided state, while the earlier question omits God sees, inferred from its later mention; this is deletion by evidence, not tanāzuʿ.
BIQAI:96:15/r2.anchor: لأنه يستدعي إضماراً والجمل لا تضمر

IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.claim: On the preceding interpretation, the condition's implied answer is that God knows and will punish the denier; this independent question denies that he is ignorant, and the condition plus answer supply the second object of arāʾayta.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r1.anchor: وعلى قولهم يتعين تقدير جواب الشرط بما يدل عليه :  { ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى } والتقدير :  إن كذب وتولى فالله عالم به

IBNASHUR:96:14/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r5.claim: The conditional predicts that Abū Jahl will deny the Prophet's call to Islam and turn away, while promising the Prophet that God will vindicate him.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r5.anchor: وفي قوله :  { إن كذب وتولى } إيذان للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن أبا جهل سيكذبه حين يدعوه إلى الإسلام وسيتولى ،  ووعد بأن الله ينتصف له منه

IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.claim: The pronouns in kadhdhaba and tawallā refer to the prohibitor in verses 9–10; context directs pronouns to their different antecedents, and the object of kadhdhaba is omitted because it is understood as the praying servant.
IBNASHUR:96:14/r6.anchor: وضمير { كذب وتولى } عائد إلى { الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } [ العلق :  9 ،  10 ]

IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:9/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:10/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNATIYYA:96:11/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:11/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:11/r2.claim: The three interrogative challenges are arranged in sequence; the closing question supplies their omitted, expansive completions and one concise threat suffices for all.
IBNATIYYA:96:11/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNATIYYA:96:12/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:12/r2.speaker: author

IBNATIYYA:96:12/r2.anchor: فجاء بها في نسق ، ثم جاء بالوعيد الكافي لجميعها اختصاراً واقتضاباً

IBNATIYYA:96:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r1.claim: Arayta is an interrogative challenge and, unlike knowledge-based vision, does not take two objects.
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { أرأيت } توقيف ، وهو فعل لا يتعدى إلى مفعولين على حد الرؤية

IBNATIYYA:96:13/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r3.claim: The denier who turns away is the person forbidding the prayer, Abu Jahl.
IBNATIYYA:96:13/r3.anchor: وقوله : { إن كذب وتولى } ، يعني الإنسان الذي ينهى

IBNATIYYA:96:14/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:14/r2.speaker: author

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl tried to stop Muhammad praying and boasted of his council; al-ʿAlaq 96:10–13 was revealed, and Ibn Abbas says angels would seize him if he summoned them.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3044/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " جاء أبو جهل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI:96:13/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:13/r1.claim: The person who denies and turns away is Abu Jahl.

MAWARDI:96:13/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:13/r2.claim: One interpretation is that he denied God and turned away from obeying Him.
MAWARDI:96:13/r2.anchor: أحدهما : كذب بالله ، وتولى عن طاعته .

MAWARDI:96:13/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:13/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:13/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that he denied the Qurʾan and turned away from faith.
MAWARDI:96:13/r3.anchor: الثاني : كذب بالقرآن ، وتولى عن الإيمان .

MAWARDI:96:13/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:13/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:13/r4.claim: A further possibility is that he denied the Messenger and refused acceptance.
MAWARDI:96:13/r4.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثاً : كذب بالرسول ، وتولى عن القبول .

NASAFI:96:13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:13/r1.claim: The alternative is that the forbidding person denies the truth and turns away from it, as Nasafī says he does.
NASAFI:96:13/r1.anchor: أرأيت إن كان ذلك الناهي مكذباً بالحق متولياً عنه كما نقول نحن

NASAFI:96:14/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:14/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:14/r2.claim: “The one who forbids” and the conditional clause are the two objects of the first “Have you seen?”; its omitted answer is supplied from the second condition, while the repeated question adds emphasis.
NASAFI:96:14/r2.anchor: { الذى ينهى } مع الجملة الشرطية مفعولا { أَرَأَيْتَ }

QURTUBI:96:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:13/r1.claim: Abu Jahl denied God's Book and turned away from belief.
QURTUBI:96:13/r1.anchor: يعني أبا جهل كذب بكتاب الله عز وجل ، وأعرض عن الإيمان .

QURTUBI:96:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:13/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:96:13/r2.claim: Al-Farra connects the clauses: the forbidden servant may be guided and command piety while the forbidding man denies and turns from the Reminder; the sequence marvels at this, then reproaches Abu Jahl for not knowing God sees and knows his act.
QURTUBI:96:13/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء : المعنى " أرأيت الذي ينهى . عبدا إذا صلى " وهو على الهدى

QURTUBI:96:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:13/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:13/r3.claim: Another grammatical view makes each later أرأيت a substitute for the first, with ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى as the predicate.
QURTUBI:96:13/r3.anchor: وقيل : كل واحد من " أرأيت " بدل من الأول . و " ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى " الخبر .

RAZI:96:13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:13/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:13/r1.claim: One reading addresses the Prophet: the proofs are evident, and sound reason recognizes that denying them and preventing worship is false and stubborn; should awareness that God sees not deter the offender?
RAZI:96:13/r1.anchor: القول الأول : أنه خطاب مع الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ، وذلك لأن الدلائل التي ذكرها في أول هذه السورة جلية ظاهرة

RAZI:96:13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:13/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:13/r2.claim: A second reading addresses the disbeliever: if Muhammad is lying or turning away, does he not know that God sees, so that he needs your prohibition?
RAZI:96:13/r2.anchor: إن كان يا كافر محمد كاذبا أو متوليا
